memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Moses said to the assembly, 'This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.'" - Lev 8:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses did as the LORD commanded. That phrase, or something close to it, will appear seven times in this chapter. Watch for it.

Repetition on this scale is deliberate. God is establishing something in Israel's memory: everything about this priesthood came from Him. Not one detail was Moses' idea.

And notice what Moses says to the crowd. He does not say, "Here is what we have decided," or "This is our tradition." He says: This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.

That is the posture of a faithful servant. Moses had enormous authority — he had confronted Pharaoh, parted a sea, climbed Sinai. And he consistently pointed away from himself.

Compare John the Baptist, who had crowds coming to him and said, He must become greater; I must become less (Jn 3:30). Or Paul: What, after all, is Apollos? And what is Paul? Only servants, through whom you came to believe (1 Cor 3:5).

The test of any spiritual leader is simple. Do they draw people toward themselves, or toward God?

And there is a personal test in it too. When you give advice, teach a class, or lead a family devotion — whose word are you actually offering?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When I speak about spiritual things, do I point people to God or to myself?
2. Am I willing to do things God's way even when I would arrange them differently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let me be a servant who points away from myself. Help me to say and do what You have commanded, not what I would prefer. Amen.
